::: {#def-local-tie-formation .theorem}
## Local tie formation

A bipartite graph generator satisfies local tie formation if the equation of each dyad depends on the rest of the system only through a bounded summary $c_{ki}$ of the person’s history, a bounded summary $c_{kl}$ of the place’s history, and a bounded summary $s_{k,il}$ of the dyad’s past, for example whether the person attended the place in the previous period:

$$
D_{k,il}=f_{\psi,k}\big(c_{ki},c_{kl},s_{k,il},U_{k,il}\big),\qquad c_{kl}=\kappa^{\mathcal{Q}}_k\big(\bar X_{k-1,l},\bar g_{k-1,l}\big),\qquad s_{k,il}=\sigma_k\big(\bar D_{k-1,il}\big),
$$

with $c_{ki}$ as in C.29, and $\kappa^{\mathcal{Q}}_k$ and $\sigma_k$ the same for every place and every dyad. $(c_{ki},c_{kl},s_{k,il})$ takes finitely many values. A row of such a generator is the collection of its dyads’ equations.
:::
